To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the maxima of a set of n points in the plane can be found in O(n log n) time using the standard plane-sweep algorithm, 2) a new algorithm finds maxima in O(n) expected time when the points are chosen uniformly at random in a general planar region, and 3) the same algorithm can be used sequentially, and is very efficient for practical use.
the expected complexity of finding the maxima in the plane is n+O(1), and that the sequential algorithm has a complexity of O(1) for each input point, with a small constant.

we give a simple classification of maxima-finding methods, propose several new maxima-finders, and show that the expected complexity of finding the maxima for uniformly chosen points from a general planar region is n+O(1).
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of locating the maxima of a set of points in the plane.
the problem of finding maxima in a set of random points in the plane.
the problem of finding the maxima in a set of points in the plane.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the best algorithm for the problem of finding maxima in random planar samples is the sequential algorithm.
the best maxima-finding methods for planar samples are those of [1, 2, 4, 7, 8, 11, 14].
the best known algorithms for maxima-finding in random planar regions are the ones proposed here.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the problem of finding the maxima in random planar samples is very well understood.
, for random planar point sets, we give a maxima-finding procedure with complexity O(√n\ln n), and a procedure with complexity O(n\ln\ln n), both being the best known in the literature.
we give a complete solution to a long standing open question of computational geometry.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the complexity of maxima-finding is essentially linear for random planar point sets.
maxima-finding is an easy problem when points are uniformly distributed in a planar region.
the complexity of the maxima-finding problem can be significantly reduced when the input is random, in comparison with the deterministic setting.
